zh.title: 英國航空BA295飛越愛爾蘭海期間客艙失壓　777緊急下降後折返倫敦
zh.summary: 英國航空BA295於10月5日飛越愛爾蘭海期間發生客艙失壓，777-200ER緊急下降至約9,000英尺後折返倫敦希斯洛，最終安全落地。
body: 英國航空（British Airways）一架原定由倫敦飛往芝加哥的波音777-200ER客機，10月5日在飛越愛爾蘭海期間發生客艙失壓，機組隨即執行緊急下降並折返英國，最終安全返回倫敦希斯洛機場（LHR）。涉事航班為BA295，目的地為芝加哥歐海爾國際機場（ORD），執飛航空器註冊編號G-VIIA。
根據飛航紀錄，G-VIIA當時巡航於約36,000英尺高度，飛至愛爾蘭海、都柏林以南約40海里處時發生客艙壓力流失。機組隨即開始緊急下降，客艙內旅客氧氣面罩亦自動釋放，飛機約7分鐘後下降至9,000英尺，平均下降率約每分鐘3,800英尺。航班追蹤資料亦顯示，BA295期間曾使用代表一般緊急狀況的7700電碼。
民航客機在高空飛行時，客艙會透過增壓系統維持適合人體活動的壓力環境；若客艙壓力無法維持，飛行員通常會迅速下降至較低高度，以確保機上人員能獲得足夠氧氣。此次BA295下降至約9,000英尺後停止下降，並取消原定跨大西洋航程，轉向返回倫敦。
由於這架777執行長程跨大西洋航班時攜帶大量燃油，折返後並未立即降落。飛機在英國西南部及布里斯托海峽一帶持續飛行以降低落地重量；航空事故紀錄顯示，該機期間亦進行放油程序，之後返回希斯洛並於27L跑道安全落地，距離開始緊急下降約4小時5分鐘。
英國航空證實，BA295因「技術問題」返回希斯洛，飛機安全降落，旅客其後正常下機，航空公司並安排受影響旅客後續行程。截至目前，英航尚未對外公布造成客艙失壓的具體技術原因。
G-VIIA為波音777-236ER，屬英國航空777-200ER機隊。Flightradar24的航班紀錄確認，該機於10月5日執行BA295倫敦—芝加哥航班；目前可查得的航空事故與航班追蹤資料亦均將此次事件記錄為BA295，因此部分網路報導使用的「BA259」航班號與飛航紀錄不符。

en.title: British Airways BA295 Suffers Cabin Depressurization Over Irish Sea, 777 Makes Emergency Descent and Returns to London
en.summary: British Airways flight BA295 suffered a cabin depressurization over the Irish Sea on October 5. The Boeing 777-200ER descended rapidly to about 9,000 feet before returning safely to London Heathrow.
body: A British Airways Boeing 777-200ER operating from London to Chicago suffered a cabin depressurization while crossing the Irish Sea on October 5, prompting the crew to make an emergency descent and return to the United Kingdom. The aircraft landed safely at London Heathrow Airport (LHR). The flight was BA295, bound for Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD), and was operated by G-VIIA.

Flight records indicate that G-VIIA was cruising at around 36,000 feet when cabin pressure was lost over the Irish Sea, roughly 40 nautical miles south of Dublin. The crew immediately initiated an emergency descent, while passenger oxygen masks deployed in the cabin. The aircraft descended to about 9,000 feet in roughly seven minutes, averaging approximately 3,800 feet per minute. Tracking data also shows that BA295 used transponder code 7700, which indicates a general emergency.

Commercial aircraft operating at high altitude rely on cabin pressurization systems to maintain a breathable environment for passengers and crew. If cabin pressure cannot be maintained, pilots typically descend rapidly to a lower altitude where sufficient oxygen is available. In this case, BA295 leveled off at around 9,000 feet and abandoned its planned transatlantic crossing before turning back toward London.

Because the 777 was carrying a large fuel load for a long-haul transatlantic flight, it did not land immediately after turning back. The aircraft remained airborne over southwestern England and the Bristol Channel area to reduce landing weight. Aviation incident records indicate that the aircraft also dumped fuel before returning to Heathrow, where it landed safely on runway 27L about four hours and five minutes after the emergency descent began.

British Airways confirmed that BA295 returned to Heathrow because of a 'technical issue.' The aircraft landed safely, passengers disembarked normally, and the airline arranged onward travel for those affected. British Airways has not yet publicly disclosed the specific technical cause of the depressurization.

G-VIIA is a Boeing 777-236ER and part of British Airways' 777-200ER fleet. Flightradar24 records confirm that the aircraft operated BA295 from London to Chicago on October 5. Available incident and flight-tracking records consistently identify the flight as BA295, meaning some online reports that referred to 'BA259' do not match the recorded flight data.
